recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow gas simulation (at minimum a Fluid **Domain** plus one **Flow** emitter), bake the cache, and render the resulting volume grids using a volume shader configured for fire: primarily **Principled Volume** with **Blackbody** emission driven by the simulation’s **temperature** (and optionally **flame**) volume attributes. For shading control, you can also use the **Volume Info** node outputs (Density/Flame/Temperature) to drive a Blackbody/Principled Volume setup.

mantaflow_workflow_minimum: Create a Fluid Domain (simulation bounds) before baking
Create one or more Flow objects to emit smoke/gas inside the Domain
(Optional) Add Effectors/force fields to shape motion
Assign a material to the Domain for volume rendering
Bake the Cache to generate voxel data used for playback/rendering

principled_volume_relevant_inputs.blackbody_intensity: Set to 1 for physically accurate intensity (per Principled Volume docs)
principled_volume_relevant_inputs.temperature_kelvin: Higher values emit more (per Principled Volume docs)
principled_volume_relevant_inputs.emission_strength: Controls emitted light amount (per Principled Volume docs)

volume_info_node_outputs.density: Scalar density of smoke inside the Fluid Domain
volume_info_node_outputs.flame: Scalar density of fire inside the Fluid Domain
volume_info_node_outputs.temperature: Scalar temperature; values 0–1 map to 0–1000 kelvin (per Volume Info docs)

volume_shading_notes.principled_volume: Recommended general-purpose physically-based volume shader; supports scattering/absorption/emission; fire can be rendered with blackbody emission
volume_shading_notes.custom_shader_option: Use Attribute node(s) to fetch grids such as density/color/temperature when building a custom volume shader

Remember the simulation workflow order matters: Domain must exist before baking; save the blend-file before baking; changes to domain/flow settings generally require re-baking (noted in the retrieved workflow text).
Volume Info Temperature is normalized: 0–1 maps to 0–1000 kelvin; if you need hotter fire shading you may need to scale/remap this value in shading (implied by the mapping statement).
alternative_approaches: Use a custom volume shader network instead of Principled Volume by combining Volume Absorption/Scatter/Emission and driving them via volume attributes (density/color/temperature) fetched with nodes like Attribute/Volume Info (per volume shading docs).
Drive blackbody-style fire using the Volume Info node’s Temperature output (0–1 mapped to kelvin) feeding a Blackbody/Principled Volume setup (per Volume Info + volume shading docs).
